clue.text: Commit oneself irrevocably to fire tramps and drifters?

definitions.meaning: to take a step that leaves no way of retreating or changing one's mind
tramps (tramp steamers) and drifters (herring boats) are both vessels, so setting fire to them literally torches your craft

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to set light to a group of vagrants and wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramps and drifters' look like homeless people, but a tramp is a cargo ship with no fixed route and a drifter is a fishing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from invaders burning their ships so retreat was impossible, hence total commitment.

clue.text: Adviser on way to dine in footballer's club

indicators.note: in places the word for dining inside the footballer's club phrase

parts.note: a back is a defender in football, with the possessive giving an S
a driver is a golf club
to dine means to eat

explanation.surface: A consultant is heading off to have dinner at a football player's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a social venue but is the golf club, DRIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger who keeps telling the driver which route to take gives unwanted advice on the road.

clue.text: Revolting person contributing to bizarre belief

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone disgusting adds to a strange creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, but here it means rising up against authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone revolting in the sense of rising in revolt is an insurgent against authority.

clue.text: Unlike chorales possibly involving first pair of trebles

definitions.text: Unlike chorales possibly involving first pair of trebles

indicators.note: involving means the scrambled letters take in the treble pair
possibly signals the letters of chorales may be arranged differently

parts.note: the opening two letters of trebles are T and R

explanation.surface: Music unlike sung hymns might still use a couple of boy sopranos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters and 'involving' takes in the treble pair. The whole clue also describes the answer: instrumental music, not choral, though it may use trebles.
explanation.definitionFit: Music for an orchestra is instrumental, in contrast to chorales, which are hymns for voices.

clue.text: European vessel bearing fish for senior diplomat's residence …

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the vessel holds the fish within it

parts.note: MY is the abbreviation for motor yacht
a bass is a fish

explanation.surface: A Continental ship carrying a fish heads for an ambassador's home.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is the official building where an ambassador lives and works.

clue.text: … a good queen consumes fish as well

indicators.note: consumes means eats, so the queen takes the fish inside her

parts.note: Good Queen Bess was a popular name for Elizabeth I
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A kindly monarch eats some fish too.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue, but this one stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides, as an adverb, means in addition or also.

clue.text: The line a stroke to boundary goes over?

indicators.note: goes over means turns back, so the cricket shot is read in reverse

parts.note: in cricket, a six is a shot that clears the boundary without bouncing

explanation.surface: A cricketer wonders whether a shot crosses the boundary rope.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball hit over the boundary rope on the full scores SIX.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is a reference line, such as one about which something rotates or on a graph.

clue.text: Stick with this show-off, if he's an officer!

definitions.text: Stick with this show-off, if he's an officer!

parts.words: Stick with this show-off, if he's an officer!
parts.note: a short cane carried by military officers is a swagger stick, so a boastful strutter is the one wielding it

explanation.surface: Advice to tolerate a braggart provided he holds military rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick with' looks like 'stay loyal to', but the stick is the officer's swagger cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A boastful person who struts about is a braggart, and officers' canes are named after that strut.

clue.text: Show confidence — mug principal of own school

parts.note: to mug is to rob someone in the street, a hold-up
the principal of your own school is your head teacher, one's head

explanation.surface: A pupil is told to rob their own headteacher as a display of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a head or headteacher runs a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping one's head held high is an idiom for appearing proud and unashamed.

clue.text: Die-shaped compartment Lebanese extremists rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a cubicle is a small partitioned compartment

indicators.note: extremists points to the outermost letters of Lebanese

explanation.surface: A Lebanese militant group refuses a box-shaped cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of Lebanese, L and E, are taken from CUBICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A die is a cube, so something shaped like one is cube-like.

clue.text: Criminal ring encompassing southern girl's beating

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the bad word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: criminal means bad
Tina is a girl's name
a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A gang of crooks surrounds a woman from the south and beats her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal ring' looks like one phrase, a gang, but it splits into BAD and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastinado is a punishment of beating the soles of the feet with a stick.

clue.text: Cut of meat sea cook served before party

indicators.note: served before places the cook's name ahead of the party

parts.note: Long John Silver is the ship's cook in Treasure Island
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A ship's cook dishes up food before a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a British cut of beef from the outer thigh, often salted.

clue.text: Very old artist briefly making comeback

indicators.note: making comeback means the word returns, read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Degas was a French impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly painter in short form stages a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims DEGAS to DEGA, then 'making comeback' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, having lived a long time.

clue.text: Source of drink yet carried in long trains?

indicators.note: carried in means placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it, so long means die
still means yet, as in still to come
RY is short for railway, which runs trains

explanation.surface: Passengers on lengthy rail journeys carry something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long trains' looks like a description of railway carriages, but 'long' is a verb here: to long is to be dying for.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillery makes spirits such as whisky, so it is where drink comes from.

clue.text: How experts act, properly protecting the lower classes

indicators.note: protecting means shielding, so the word for properly surrounds the classes

parts.note: aptly means properly or suitably
D and E are the lowest grades in British social classification

explanation.surface: Specialists behave correctly while shielding the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades social classes A, B, C1, C2, D and E; D and E are the lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts behave skilfully, which is to act in a proficient manner.

clue.text: Tense term, having reorganised course

indicators.note: having reorganised says the letters of tense term are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammarian rearranges a tense-related term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a course of a meal, not a study course.
explanation.definitionFit: An entremets is a dessert or side dish served between main courses of a meal.

clue.text: Support prison riot at first, appearing in court

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of riot

parts.note: to be up before the judge is to appear in court

explanation.surface: A prison disturbance leads to defendants facing a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup supports a rider's foot hanging from a saddle.

clue.text: Take away last of freight conveyed from east to west

indicators.note: from east to west in an across clue means reading right to left

parts.note: carted means conveyed or transported

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of freight

explanation.surface: A goods shipment is moved across the country from one coast to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to take away from or diminish something's value.

clue.text: Learner encountered bad weather in driving area

indicators.note: in places the weather inside the driving area

parts.note: the tee is where golfers drive off
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: A novice motorist runs into a storm on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving area' suggests roads, but it is the golfer's tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone being taught a job, a learner.

clue.text: Long-serving archdeacon receiving new rate

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the title wraps round the anagram

parts.note: an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, Ven

indicators.note: new signals the letters of rate in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman is given a fresh pay scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the anagram of rate, which the archdeacon's title takes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long experience, here used adjectivally.

clue.text: Examination originally required in all animal study centres

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination

indicators.note: originally means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A test is first needed in every zoological research lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaria are enclosures where animals are kept under natural conditions for observation.

clue.text: Plato's Form is almost perfect

indicators.note: almost means nearly complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A philosopher's concept is nearly flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: Plato called his perfect Forms ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: In Platonic philosophy the eternal Forms are also called Ideas.

clue.text: Old American poet initially causing great wonder

indicators.note: initially means the poet's name comes first

parts.note: Andrew Marvell was an English poet

explanation.surface: An early American poet initially arouses awe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old American poet' reads as one person, but it splits: the poet is the English Marvell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marvellous is wonderful, arousing astonishment.

clue.text: In middle of zoo I tease a small antelope

indicators.note: in middle of means take the central letter of zoo

parts.note: to rib is to tease

explanation.surface: In a zoo I make fun of a little deer-like animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope.

clue.text: City district accommodating religious, blockbuster

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the district holds the other piece

parts.note: EC is a London postal district covering the City
pi is slang for pious, religious

explanation.surface: An urban district houses a devout film.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long, lavish film, the kind of blockbuster studios produce.

clue.text: Unexpected revelation always restricting the old championship

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the word for always surrounds the others

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever
ye is an old form of the
an Open is a championship, as in golf or tennis

explanation.surface: Something surprising is that the old tournament is always limited.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is something surprising that reveals the truth.

clue.text: English team the French officially banish

parts.note: XI is eleven, a football or cricket team
le is French for the

explanation.surface: France officially expels an English sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile is to expel someone from their country by order.

clue.text: Flyer's unrevealed lines about a spell in jail (9,4) 23,031

parts.note: secret means unrevealed
RY, railway, means lines
bird is slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: An aviator's undisclosed railways connect to a jail term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' is a bird: the African secretary bird. BIRD is rhyming slang (bird-lime, time) for a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The secretary bird is a long-legged African bird of prey that flies.
